brief.subject: EUDR Brief: EU forest cover data and cocoa supply shifts
brief.headline: EU forest cover holds near 39% as Commission keeps EUDR in focus
brief.dek: New Commission land and habitat figures, a Commissioner at an EUDR event, and a cocoa replacer pitched against supply risk.
brief.lede: The Commission says EU forest cover has stabilised at approximately 39% of land. That baseline frames the EUDR's push to curb deforestation linked to imports.

sections.heading: EU land and forest snapshot
bullets: Forest covers approximately 39% of EU land and has stabilised, according to the Commission's environment newsroom.
Protected areas make up 26.4% of total EU land, showing how much territory falls under conservation rules.
81% of protected EU habitats are in poor or bad condition, a figure that underlines the environmental case behind the EUDR.

sections.heading: Commissioner joins EUDR event
bullets: A Commissioner attended an EUDR event, the Commission's environment newsroom reported.
The item gave no remarks, dates or new guidance, so compliance teams have nothing new to act on yet.

sections.heading: Cocoa replacers target supply risk
bullets: Planet A Foods launched Cocoa Booster, a high-fiber powder that can replace up to 100% of cocoa in select applications.
The launch cites rising cocoa costs, a sign that buyers are seeking ways to reduce exposure to tight, regulated supply chains.
GLP-1-driven demand shifts are also cited, so cocoa exporters may face changing product demand alongside EUDR requirements.
